facts.text: Public administration is the main employment sector for Gatineau residents, with nearly one person in four (24.1% of the active population) working in that field.
The Gatineau sector groups 1,468 businesses, the largest number in the city, representing 42% of all commercial establishments on the territory.
Federal government policy provides for a split of federal jobs of 25% in Gatineau versus 75% in Ottawa, following the transfer of part of the public service to Hull in the early 1970s.

overview: Gatineau had 291,041 residents in the 2021 Census, up 5.4% from 276,245 in 2016, with 126,476 occupied dwellings spread over 341.84 square kilometres. Growth outpaced most Quebec cities, driven by its place in the National Capital Region.

Public administration is the dominant employer, and a large share of federal jobs in the capital region sit on the Gatineau side. A local business serves bilingual, public-sector households who also shop and compare prices across the river in Ottawa.

byService.lead-generation: Gatineau lead generation should reach bilingual public servants with French-first campaigns timed around stable pay cycles, competing against Ottawa businesses for the same 291,041 residents.
byService.seo: SEO in Gatineau must rank in French and English and target sector names like Hull, Aylmer and Buckingham, because Ottawa results otherwise dominate regional searches.
byService.website-development: A Gatineau website should launch fully bilingual, load fast on mobile and make service areas clear across the 341.84 square kilometres of merged former municipalities.
byService.branding: Gatineau branding should signal reliability and bilingual professionalism to a public-sector market whose population rose 5.4% between 2016 and 2021.
